Service Requirements The Contractor must provide printing services, including the following tasks: • Graphic design and creation of annual report content for various Embassy offices. • Graphic design and creation of brochures, information portfolios, folders, advertising publications, flyers, and similar materials for the Embassy's promotional events. • Printing and/or photocopying of documents, brochures, and portfolios in a professional manner, ensuring clear colors, photographs, text, and images for finished products. Preference will be given to contractors offering multiple printing methods, such as commercial, digital, press, and web-based printing. • Supplying stock images for publications, as needed. • Providing printing designs for requesting offices to review and confirm prior to production. The Contractor is responsible for installing, setting up, and delivering printed items to U.S. Embassy Hanoi events. • Material Requirements: The Contractor shall present several material options for the Embassy's selection prior to submitting a quote. Services must include all necessary supplies — such as equipment, toner, developer, fuser agent, staples, paper, g

insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

Website The AOC Design Standards may be found in the AOC eDocs Project Delivery Guidance site. 6 AOC Order 28-8, December 26, 2018 Section B – AOC Design Standards General Requirements Purpose: This manual establishes minimum design standards and criteria for the design, repairs, alterations, modernizations, renewals and construction of facilities under the jurisdiction of the Architect of the Capitol. This document contains technical criteria to be used in the programming, design, construction, measurement, verification and documentation of AOC facilities. This is a mandatory standard and is not a guidebook, textbook, handbook, training manual nor substitute for technical competence. It represents the AOC’s commitment to comply with the requirements of applicable law and widely accepted building codes and standards. This standard must be used in conjunction with the governing standards referenced in this document, as well as the building program for each project. If a conflict exists between these standards and a specific program and project requirements, contact Planning and Project Management for resolution. The design team must review compliance with the building program at each stage of the

throughout the planning, design, construction and occupancy of the project. Commissioning Guidelines for AOC Projects are contained in the policy statement of June 7, 2010. During the initial planning process, the AOC Project Team shall determine the purpose and role of commissioning. The purpose may be to ensure proper integration of a small renovation/rehabilitation into the Capitol 7 AOC Order 28-8, December 26, 2018 complex, or it may be related to a certification. It may range from simple, direct Owner commissioning by the AOC to an independent Commissioning Agent with a substantial budget. As a rule, if a project is designed by an Associate A/E, then commissioning will be performed by a third party hired by the AOC. Within the context of design for mechanical systems, commissioning plays a significant role. The designer of the mechanical system has these responsibilities: i. Develop and document the Program of Requirements (PoR.) ii. Develop a basis of design. Commissioning shall help ensure that mechanical systems operate properly as a holistic system. The parts and pieces must interact as required by the sequences of operation and do so within an appropriate time frame. The pre-functional and functional performance tests will verify this perform

General: The main objectives of this section are to optimize building performance and minimize adverse effects on the environment. It is the intent of this section to achieve these goals through the following measures: i. Address planning, designing and construction of new buildings and renovations or alterations to existing buildings. ii. Increase cost savings through better energy, water and material management. iii. Reduce water supply constraints and preserve a critical natural resource. iv. Access tools to encourage energy efficiency improvements. v. Empower project teams to make more informed decisions. vi. G

Life Cycle Cost Analysis: Life-cycle cost-effectiveness (LCCE) applies to this entire section unless otherwise stated. In addition to energy, water and renewables, LCCE may be applied to other materials, and building construction types. The purpose of the LCCE is to deliver buildings that meet mission needs at the lowest total ownership cost. Meters must be connected to utility monitoring and building automation system using the installation’s advanced metering protocols. The consultant/contractor shall work closely with the AOC for specific requirements. Recycled Content: The Resource Conservation and Recovery Act requires agencies to buy recycled content products designated by the EPA (EPA Comprehensive Procurement Guidelines 40 CFR part 247). For EPA designated materials, use products meeting or exceeding EPA’s recycled content requirements. For other products, design shall use materials with recycled content, such that the sum of post-consumer content constitutes at least 10 percent of the total value of the materials of the project. LE: files/Attach_1_-_Blood_Transfusion_Services_SOW.pdf ===== Statement of Work For Transfusion Services 20 October 2026 I. Background: The 88th Medical Group Transfusion Services requires blood components and references lab transfusion testing services. The supplier shall provide blood products and reference blood transfusion services (testing) to support the blood supply in case of emergency situations and inpatient and outpatient care at the WPAFB Medical Center when requested for a period of 5 years at the prices in the approved price list. II. Minimum Technical Requirements: The supplier shall provide blood products and reference transfusion testing that are time dependent with immediate response and expedience to treat critical patients. The supplier must operate 24/7 as the 88th Medical Group (MDG) is a 24/7 operation; this service must be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays and weekends. The supplier shall provide rapid shipment of blood products when the 88 MDG Transfusion Services in-house inventory is in need to support critical patients. The one-hour turnaround time for testing is a mission-critical requirement. The blood supplier shall deliver routine blood products ordered on a STAT basis within one (1) hour of the blood sup

eipt of an emergent request for blood products. The required completion point is delivery to the Transfusion Services department. The supplier must fulfill our request with the ordered product with appropriate compatible blood type, applicable testing, and requested quantities. Any unforeseen delays are understandable; however, the ultimate goal is for the delivering agency to aim for the <1 hour delivery time. An appropriate transmittal list is required with each delivery. If emergent requests are unable to be consistently met, it could mean critical failure for our hospital's life-saving capabilities. The supplier shall have 24/7 reference laboratory testing capabilities for patients anticipating transfusions or medical treatment. The supplier must be licensed by the Food & Drug Administration (FDA) and follow American Association of Blood Bank (AABB) standards. The supplier must notify the 88th MDG Transfusion Services of all unexpected/abnormal tests from blood products supplied by them. The supplier shall provide look-back notifications to the 88th MDG as required by 21 CFR 610.48 (b)(3): (a) within three (3) calendar days if blood collected from a donor who tested negative at the time of donation but tests reactive for evidence of HIV or HCV infection on a later do
